Definition: from G4862 and εἶμι (to go); to assemble:--gather together.
BiblicalUsage: When much people are gathered together and come to Jesus out of every city, He speaks to them by a parable, and Paul, blinded on the Damascus road, is led by the hand of those who are with him. Being with others is the ordinary shape of the gospel: crowds gather to hear, and friends lead the blind.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the gospel gathers people together, and I hold that being with Christ's people is often how the blind find their way.
